relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease: 'This test identified a de novo missense variant, c.1126C>T, in GFAP'; the Discussion also summarizes five previously published p.R376W carriers.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script assembled the JSON from hand-written values and checked every span verbatim. Scope: the proband ('patient'); his parents, who were tested by cosegregation analysis ('mother of patient', 'father of patient'; described as 'female' and 'male' to whom he was born; no variant rows because the variant was de novo); and five previously published p.R376W carriers summarized in the Discussion (refs 34-37), each with at least one individual-level fact; the mother-son pair from ref 34 is labelled 'ref 34 patient' and 'son of ref 34 patient'. Figure 4A tabulates these five cases but is an image; nothing was read from it beyond its legend. Three older siblings (proband is 'the fourth child') are not described individually and get no rows. Variant fields for the five prior cases: only the protein string p.R376W is printed for them; variant type, zygosity, pathogenicity and functional evidence are left 'not reported' for them (the paper's statements describe the proband's c.1126C>T); the son's inheritance is 'inherited maternal' from the Figure 4 legend stating mother and son both harbor p.R376W. Proband zygosity not stated for him (only a general statement that most GFAP variants are heterozygous), so 'not reported'. The transcript NM_002055.4 is printed in the Introduction sentence that introduces the proband's c.1126C>T. Pathogenicity: testing laboratory called it a VUS; authors reclassify it as pathogenic citing ACMG 2015 but print no criteria codes. Proband: 'relative macrocephaly' is hedged ('suggestive of', head circumference at the 89th percentile) but recorded as observed; 'probable lactate elevation' is hedged. 'There were no concerns regarding early developmental delay' (neonatal period) vs later 'concern for developmental delay' and developmental delay in the abstract: read as a time course, not a contradiction; developmental delay recorded observed. Checklist dysphagia for the proband is from the swallow study (premature spillage, delayed swallow); 'protracted vomiting' mapped to 'recurrent vomiting'. 'no signs of regression' recorded as a feature row (regression excluded) but not used to exclude 'cognitive decline'. Normal/negative findings (EEG normal, extensive workup negative, VLCFA and uric acid 'essentially normal', Apgar unremarkable) recorded as excluded abnormalities; the extensive workup is a whole investigation and is written as the paper lists it, excluding nothing more specific. Age at last evaluation for the proband is the '19-month-old' age at panel testing given in the Introduction (the oldest age stated); age at diagnosis not stated. Consanguinity 'no' is from 'There was no report of consanguinity'. Vital status not stated for anyone. Ref 37 patient: 'Until presentation, development was normal' recorded as developmental delay excluded (time-limited). Ref 34 patient: 'palatal myoclonus' mapped to checklist 'palatal tremor', 'ocular myoclonus' to eye movement abnormality; 'brainstem' lesions not used for the medulla item. n_patients_reported = 1 from 'we report on a patient' (the five literature cases are summaries). No stacked cells; no in-paper contradictions found.
